Level Objectives B1
At the end of the level:
1. unpack the regular words in root and pattern and find them in the dictionary by root;
2. use the verbal forms I/X, the parties, the maṣdar and the passive, even weak verbs;
3. build sentences with ḥāl, tamyīz, absolute complement, hypothetical period, exception, numerals and dates;
4. read short news without vowels (150–300 words) with the dictionary and make them in English with precision, respecting sources and degrees of certainty;
5. read in silence a news without vowels at least 70 words per minute and report their contents;
6. understand simplified news and the main points of authentic news on known topics; write a dictation with at least the85% correct words;
7. write a faithful summary of 100–120 words and a formal letter of 120–150 words;
8. support a spontaneous conversation on family and topical issues, asking for clarification and arguing;

9. In Egyptian you can manage in everyday situations, express opinions and follow a simple scene with subtitles Arabs. These are internal objectives of the course, written on the model of the descriptors of the Common European Framework for Level B1. Passing the exam B1 does not amount to CEFR certification (see "Seals and Evaluation").

blocks.text: The Egyptian Track

In A2-24 You filled out the decision form on the dialect. The default choice of the course is the Egyptian of Cairo: it is the most understood variety in the Arab world thanks to cinema, television and music, has many teaching materials and is close to fuṣḥā in many facilities. The EGY track occupies about the 20–25% of the time: ten units of six weeks each (seven last), studied in blocks separated from the standard Arabic, not to mix the two systems. That's what you spell. The Egyptian is written in Arabic characters without vowels, as the Egyptians write in their messages, with the transliteration next door. In transliteration: g per ⁧ج⁩ , ʾ for the ⁧ق⁩ pronounced as hamza, ē and ō for long vowels born from ay and aw. Who reads the scripts. Egyptian scripts should be read by an Egyptian speaker (tutor, tandem partner): vocal synthesis does not pronounce the dialect reliably. If you've chosen another variety. If in the tab of A2-24 you have chosen, for example, the Levantine, the standard Arabic units remain identical; the EGY track should be replaced with an equivalent path for that variety, to be requested separately. In the meantime, EGY units can be used as recognition exercises.
The tracks ONO and INT

ONO-03 completes the volume onomastics track 3 with the names of states, regions, cities and entities, their transliteration and their variants in documents. As in units ONO-01 and ONO-02, a name says something about the conventions of a language and a country, not about the person or place: it is never used to deduce the origin, religion or opinions of someone. INT-01 and INT-02 open the specialist module, which will continue in subsequent levels. They teach a language method to work on public sources: to recognize who says what and with what degree of certainty, to distinguish facts and opinions, to document sources, to translate prudently, to know the vocabulary of institutions. Track rules apply throughout the course: only open and public sources; no search for information on private citizens; no false identities and no access to non-public spaces; exercises on uncontested topics and invented cases; no operational procedures. The track does not replace vocational training or the rules of service.

In EGY units, dialogues have three columns (Egyptian, Transliteration, Translation). Symbols. ★ in the vocabulary indicates a high frequency word to be used actively. ⁧◌⁩ indicates a space to be completed. " (Recognize) " means a form to be understood but not yet to be produced. Arabic and Italian on the same line. Arabic can be read from right to left even inside an Italian sentence. When multiple Arabic words are separated only by spaces or punctuation, the layout sets them as a single Arabic phrase; where they are separated by ...................................................................................................................................................................................................................................................................................................... Invented texts. People, companies, news, letters and cases of the volume are invented and serve only for didactic purposes: the news is authentic in style and does not describe actual facts, and the cases at the police station do not describe operational procedures. When a text contains real information (a city, a monument, an institution), the text or solution says so.
Method

The standard week (standard rhythm, 60 minutes a day): 10 minutes of active booster review, 30 lessons and exercises, 20 reading, listening or writing; in two of the seven days, instead of the standard Arabic lesson, a block of 40–45 Egyptian minutes. In addition, one or two sessions a week with the tutor. At a light pace every week of the calendar lasts two real weeks; At an intensive pace, the extra time goes to reading, listening authentically and conversation, not to anticipating unity. How a unit is made. The standard Arabic units have 22 sections: tab (code, level, prerequisites, time, materials, objectives, plan), two dialogues, explanations with tables, pronunciation, new vocabulary with root, category, gender and plural, examples in context, graduated exercises, readings, a translation from Arabic to English with the column of Accuracy, writing, listening (with dictation), oral production, errors typical of italophones, review to active recall, final verification and criteria to move to the next unit. EGY units have 17 sections, with systematic comparison with the fuṣḥā. I'm going back without Anki. The active callback review is an Italian → Arabic table: cover the right column, answer aloud, then check. Redo the table of the previous unit at the beginning of each new unit, and those of the weak units in the bearing weeks. For the vocabulary, use Appendix B by covering the Arabic column; Mark in the notebook the forgotten words and write for each one a sentence of your own. Exercises and solutions. Always answer in writing before looking at the solutions. In tutor mode the exercises arrive one at a time and the solution is not shown before your answer, except your request. I'm listening. The course does not contain audio recordings. Each listener has a script: ask another person to read it, or paste it into an Arabic synthesizer app without reading it first. Voice synthesis can make mistakes in vowels, endings and some consonants: the pronunciation of reference is that of the tutor. From the module B1.3 add to the script graduated and authentic news (B1-18, Appendix C); from the end of the EGY track, authentic scenes and Egyptian films with Arab subtitles (EGY-10). The dictionary by root becomes in B1 the daily instrument (B1-01). In the tests and exams it is only allowed in the translation test.

Stories. The criteria in the tests range from 1 a 4 (Accessibility, Organization and lexicon or register, Fluidity and interaction or pronunciation); in the examination by 1 a 5, to have more steps in the long tests. The translation always has two criteria: Accuracy (the sense, the degrees of certainty, the times) and, in the exam, Resa in English. The pronunciation and interaction evaluates a native language tutor: without tutor the oral part remains unfinished and does not replace with a self-assessment. What does a passed exam say? The exams of the course are self-correct or correct by the tutor: they attest that you have mastered the studied program, not that you possess a certified CEFR level. The end of the B1 is a good time for external feedback before an independent examiner: the possibilities, with verified information, are in Appendix C.

Studying with the tutor
For a guided session, write "Session" followed by the unit code (e.g. "Session" B1-17EGY Session-06() and paste the last line of the register. The session always follows the same steps:
1. short recovery of the previous unit;
2. 3–5 quick questions about what you should already know;
3. explanation of the new topic with examples;
4. exercises one at a time, with the solution only after your answer;
5. correction with cause of error and a consolidation exercise;
6. updated log line and targeted review for the following days.

In B1 serve 1–2 sessions per week with a native speaker teacher, even online, and if possible an Egyptian tandem partner: for conversation, pronunciation, correction of summaries and letters, script reading and oral testing of tests and exams.
The progress log

This volume does not have an Excel file: keep the log on your notebook or spreadsheet, with one line per week. Recommended columns: date, calendar week, standard Arabic units, EGY units, unit verification score, test section scores, address book criteria, timed reading words per minute, dictation percentage, study time, error notes. It is the source of truth of your path, independent from any platform memory, and it is the basis of the profile by skill of B1-24.
